chunks: ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a mat whose reeds had been moistened with impure water: is salat (prayer) permissible upon it? So he said:
If it has dried, then there is no harm in performing salat (prayer) upon it.

key_terms.الْبَارِيَّةِ: a mat, specifically a woven reed mat
key_terms.جُفِّفَتْ: it was dried or became dry
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection
key_terms.قَصَبُهَا: its reeds, the material from which the mat is made

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray on a reed mat that was wetted with impure water after it dries?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about praying on a reed mat that had been wetted with impure water. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that once it has dried, there is no harm in praying on it, indicating the practical effect of dryness in this case for salat (prayer).
